$why: Operator, 2026-10-01 (a story spanning a shared library and the codelines that consume it): shared
changes MUST be treated differently, the run must mirror what a developer faces, and it is the
detective's judgement, not engine rules. The spec said the consumers needed no edit because their
declared range 'picks it up'; the library was a major version past every consumer's range.
Appended to the detective's prescription only when its story spans more than one codeline, so a
story confined to one codeline is asked exactly what it was asked before.

Operator, 2026-10-06: a consumer's declared range is never changed by a story ('avoid package.json upgrades in this change'; a range may be locked for a reason); the provider ships the change on a release line inside each consumer's range.
description: Composed into the code-graph detective's prescription for a story that spans codelines: say whether a fix site is shared between them, and whether each consumer's declared range takes the change.
body:
THIS STORY SPANS CODELINES. You are investigating codeline "__THIS_CODELINE__"; the same story is also being worked in: __OTHER_CODELINES__.
__CODELINE_PACKAGES__
SAY WHETHER A FIX SITE IS SHARED — add "shared" to a fix site when the change lives in, or depends on a change to, a package that one of these codelines PROVIDES and another CONSUMES. A change to a shared package is not finished when its own repository builds: every consumer receives it only through the version range it declares, so a change that ships in a version outside a consumer's range never reaches that consumer, however correct it is. Read the facts, do not assume them: this codeline's own manifest says what it provides (its name and version) or which range of a package it consumes, and what is actually installed. Where PACKAGE FACTS are given above, they are read from the manifests and are authoritative: shipsInVersion is the providing codeline's version there unless this change must ship in a different one, and a consumer judges receivesChange by comparing its declared range with it. Where they are not given, the codeline that PROVIDES the package states shipsInVersion from its own manifest; a consumer never assumes its range will take the change.

  "shared": {"package":"<the package name, as its manifest declares it>","providedBy":"<the codeline that provides it>","shipsInVersion":"<the version the provider's change will ship in, read from the provider's own manifest; empty when you cannot read it>","consumers":[{"codeline":"<a codeline that consumes it>","declaredRange":"<the range that codeline's manifest declares, or \"unknown\" when you cannot read it>","receivesChange":<true if that range takes the version this change ships in, false if it does not, null if you cannot tell>}],"note":"<one line: what a consumer must do to build and test against this change>"}

Omit "shared" on a site that touches nothing another of these codelines provides or consumes — that is the common case. A consumer's declared range of a shared package is NEVER changed by this story: moving it is that consumer's own migration (across a major version it is a breaking upgrade), not part of this change. If a consumer cannot receive the change through its declared range, say so with receivesChange:false and name the remedy in the PROVIDER: a fix site that also ships the change on a release line inside that consumer's range — cut from the newest release the range already takes, shipping as the next version on that line — and state that version as the consumer's shipsInVersion. Never name a consumer's manifest entry as a fix site. A consumer whose only remaining change was its range has no manifest edit; describe what it still needs in its own code, or that it receives the change unedited once the in-range release is installed.
__SIBLING_SHARED__
